solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor on land makes a decent feller?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: to lumber someone is to land them with an unwanted burden
Jack, short for jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman come ashore proves to be a thoroughly good chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decent' is a pun: a tree feller brings the trunk down, a descent. 'Feller' looks like slang for fellow but is someone who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcutter in the forest fells trees, so he is literally a feller.

clue.text: Exploit 26 sacked after backing international trade union

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of 26 come after the reversed pair in the answer
backing means these letters are read in reverse order, upwards in this down entry
sacked, as in a city ransacked, signals that the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the answer to 26 across is ISLE

explanation.surface: A union official is told to exploit a sacked worker after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like dismissed from a job, but here it means ransacked, so the letters of the island answer are jumbled; 'backing' turns the abbreviations round and 'after' puts the jumble last.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource is to make use of it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bust ultimately ends in boom

indicators.note: in means the picked letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means the very last letter of the word ends is taken

explanation.surface: A financial bust is just where every boom finishes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' and 'boom' look like a boom-and-bust economy; bust is the definition. 'ultimately' takes S, the end of 'ends', and 'in' puts it inside BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a woman's chest, which is also called her bosom.

clue.text: Low-profile swimmer receives more sick banter

indicators.note: receives means the fish takes the other word inside itself

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish, a swimmer with a very low profile
iller is the comparative of ill, meaning more sick

explanation.surface: A modest swimmer endures increasingly nasty teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ray is 'low-profile' because it is a flat fish that hugs the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or mockery, much the same as banter.

clue.text: Eastender's somewhat embarrassed by setback with male director

indicators.note: with joins the last piece on after the others

parts.note: a Cockney East Ender drops the H, so half, meaning somewhat, is said 'alf
an embarrassed person goes red
a hitch is a setback or snag
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A soap character from EastEnders is a bit flustered by a setback involving a man.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a London-set British TV soap; an East Ender here is a Cockney, who drops initial H, so 'half red' (somewhat embarrassed) becomes 'ALF RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the British film director famed for suspense thrillers such as Psycho.

clue.text: Core component's speaker finally replaced by new housing for woofer

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped out and the other put in its place

parts.note: a kernel is the core component of a nut or a system

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word speaker

explanation.surface: An audio engineer swaps out a core part of a speaker for a new woofer housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woofer' looks like a loudspeaker, matching 'speaker' and 'component', but here it is a dog. 'finally' takes R, the end of 'speaker', which N replaces in KERNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that woofs lives in a small hut built to house it.

clue.text: Addict requires attendant to leave hospital

indicators.note: requires the letter to leave means it is taken out of the word

parts.note: an usher is an attendant who shows people to their seats
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An addict needs a carer before being discharged from hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes drugs habitually is called a drug user, so an addict is a user.

clue.text: Where climbing plant might grow bananas or nuts

definitions.meaning: a creeper such as ivy grows climbing a vertical surface
both are slang for crazy, which this idiom also means

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on where a climber grows, followed by a fruit-and-nut aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven crazy is a British idiom for going mad, and a creeper climbs a vertical wall.

clue.text: Finish questions for the audience standing up

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as it would be heard by listeners

parts.note: whys are questions asking why

explanation.surface: A speaker ends by taking audience questions while standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the audience' says WHYS is heard, giving WISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endwise means with the end upward or forward, so an object set this way is upright.

clue.text: Mental tendency observed in brainwaves periodically

indicators.note: periodically means letters are taken at regular intervals, here every third

explanation.surface: A psychological leaning can be detected in brain-wave patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the text: every third letter of 'in brainwaves' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bias is a prejudice or leaning of the mind towards one view.

clue.text: Limitless number happy if United behind at home

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come behind, after, the short piece in the answer

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: happy, as in happy-go-lucky disorder, signals a loose rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A football report: a huge score would cheer fans if Manchester United trailed at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club but is just fodder; 'happy' is an unusual anagram signal, and 'behind' puts the jumble after the home piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitude is boundlessness, or an infinite quantity, a number without limit.

clue.text: Sadism always involves causing misery

indicators.note: involves means the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A grim moral observation that cruelty always brings suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dismal is gloomy and depressing, so it brings about wretchedness.

clue.text: Inner parts of sexy legs resist scholarly explanation

indicators.note: inner parts means each word loses its outside letters, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: An invitation to resist the inner thighs of shapely legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical interpretation of a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: Firm in favour of half that's left

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly that has set
for means in favour of, as in being for a plan

indicators.note: half means only the first part of the word that is used

explanation.surface: A company backs half of what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the leftover part of the wordplay, but it is the definition: departed. 'half' takes TH from 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to depart on a journey, so someone who did so has gone away.

clue.text: Stuffing might upset team

parts.note: force means might or power

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and reordered

explanation.surface: Stuffing your face might upset the team before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning power. 'upset' rearranges TEAM to MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a seasoned mixture of chopped meat used as a filling for poultry.

clue.text: Cross on the right of primate's crest

indicators.note: the letter is placed on the right of, after, the animal in this across answer

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A cross mark beside a monkey's head crest.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the top or peak of something, like the crest of a hill.

clue.text: Person leading by example's first to make earliest showing

indicators.note: by means placed beside, the letter following the leader

parts.note: a premier is a prime minister, a person leading a government

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word example

explanation.surface: A leader setting an example is first to attend an opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance of a film or play.

clue.text: Outstanding person supported by the Queen

parts.note: something on another thing is resting on it, supported by it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A distinguished figure enjoys royal backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a 'supported by' B, A sits on B, so ON stands for 'supported by'.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a remarkable, unique individual: one of a kind.

clue.text: Board meeting about backing VIP

indicators.note: meeting means the two pieces come together side by side
backing means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or bed and board

explanation.surface: A boardroom meeting discussing support for a very important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board meeting' looks like one phrase, but 'Board' is its own piece and 'meeting' just joins it to the reversed word for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction, a very important person.

clue.text: Time to replace lead on old radio never switching off?

indicators.note: to replace the lead on the word means its first letter is swapped for the new one

parts.note: wireless is an old-fashioned word for a radio set

explanation.surface: It's time to change the flex on an old radio that never turns off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like an electrical flex, but it means the first letter, W, which T replaces. The question mark marks the playful definition: someone never switching off is tireless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tireless person never flags or rests, as if they never power down.

clue.text: She will perform briefly in preparation for making film

parts.note: she'll is the contraction of she will

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: to act is to perform

explanation.surface: An actress will give a short performance while preparing to make a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie, but it is a thin coating; 'briefly' drops T from ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish that dries to a thin glossy coating on wood.

clue.text: Shocked at being bored by good experiences

indicators.note: being bored by means the word is drilled into, so the other pieces go inside it

parts.note: has means experiences, as in has a good time

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at being bored by pleasant experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' looks like weary, but means drilled through, so the other pieces go inside the word 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or amazement.

clue.text: AI must not be used in deployment of shattering power

indicators.note: these letters must not be used means they are removed from the pool before rearranging
deployment means the letters are arranged afresh, as troops are deployed

explanation.surface: A warning that artificial intelligence must not be used in deploying devastating force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AI' looks like artificial intelligence but is just two letters, which 'must not be used in' removes before 'deployment of' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is might or force, a plain synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Impressionist artist introduces good way to draw certain objects

indicators.note: introduces means the painter's name takes the letter into its middle

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter associated with Impressionism

explanation.surface: A painter demonstrates a good way of drawing objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like sketching, but it means attract: iron objects are pulled towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: This device attracts iron and steel items, pulling only certain metal objects towards it.

clue.text: Figure leaving university could be source of sadness

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the word before it is rearranged
could be signals that the remaining letters can be reformed into another word

explanation.surface: A student dropping out of university could cause heartache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes U from FIGURE, and 'could be' rearranges FIGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief is deep sorrow, so it is a cause and state of unhappiness.

clue.text: Old bore eating round cheese gets wind

indicators.note: eating means the outer word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Edam is a round Dutch cheese
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An old bore munching a round cheese ends up with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like flatulence, but means a wind instrument; 'eating' signals the insertion. The cheese goes in ahead of the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe d'amore is a mezzo-soprano oboe, a woodwind instrument used by Bach.

clue.text: 19 at sea possibly rest here

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder
possibly signals that the letters left over could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is TIRELESS

explanation.surface: A tireless sailor might take a break here.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove REST from TIRELESS and the leftover letters I, L, E, S are rearranged. An island at sea is where a voyager might rest, so the clue as a whole also points to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at a place in the sea, an island where a sailor could stop.

clue.text: Radical article in French newspaper

parts.note: le is the French definite article, meaning the
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: An extreme piece runs in a French newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Political radicals are associated with the progressive wing, the opposite of the right.

clue.text: Produce results with appropriate impact

parts.note: to appropriate is to take something for one's own use
an effect is an impact or influence

explanation.surface: A fitting dramatic impression yields results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective fitting, but is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that begins to work, or a rule that comes into force, starts to have its intended outcome.
